app/lib/format.ts:38-45 — latestEnglishFlavor / displayValue, pure and testable, untested
coverage_of_risk.rationale: Not a single test of the agent's own exists, so none of the risky logic (filtering, pagination, sorting, URL state, caching, not-found paths) is covered by the app itself.

evidence: app/lib — no *.test.* or __tests__ anywhere in app/
behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: There are no tests at all, so there is nothing behavioural or implementation-focused to assess.

evidence: app/lib/api.ts:17-26 — promise cache semantics (resolved nulls cached forever) unguarded
app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:96-170 — move dedup, method ordering and default-game selection unguarded
app/components/HomeBrowser.tsx:40-53 — buildHref default-param omission and page clamping unguarded
regression_power.rationale: With no app-owned tests, any refactor of the data layer or the client components regresses silently unless an acceptance spec happens to touch that exact fixture.

evidence: app/ — 0 test files, so no noise either
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no low-value padding, but also no signal; per the anchor this scores 3.

findings.issue: No test infrastructure and no app-owned tests despite large amounts of pure, easily testable logic
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest (or Playwright component tests) with unit tests for lib/format.ts and lib/api.ts and behaviour tests for HomeBrowser filtering/pagination and MovesSection sorting — these are the parts a data-layer refactor would break.

findings.issue: Filter predicates, 48-per-page slicing and page clamping (currentPage = min(max(page,1), totalPages)) are untested; off-by-one and default-omission bugs in buildHref would slip through
findings.suggestion: Characterisation tests: q/type/generation permutations, page beyond totalPages, empty-result page 1, and that buildHref omits q/type/generation/page at defaults.

findings.issue: The sort comparator's missing-values-last-in-both-directions rule, asc/desc flip, and aria-sort placement are classic regression magnets with no coverage
findings.suggestion: Table-driven tests over compareRows/sortedRows covering null power/accuracy/level, string vs numeric columns, and toggle-flip sequencing.

findings.issue: Moves-table construction (dedup key method|move|level, default game = highest order with fallback, Level Up sorted by level-then-name, method order level-up/machine/egg/tutor then alphabetical) is entirely unguarded
findings.suggestion: Integration test against a fixture pokemon record asserting table order, dedup, and selected-game fallback when ?game= is invalid.

findings.issue: cached() only evicts on promise rejection; apiFetch resolves null on any !ok response, so a transient API failure permanently caches 'not found' for a resource until restart — nothing would catch this
findings.suggestion: Unit test the cache's eviction semantics and consider evicting resolved-null entries (or treating null as a retryable miss).

findings.issue: latestEnglishFlavor (last en entry, whitespace collapsed) and displayValue (0 vs null) are spec-critical pure functions with no tests; a refactor to .find() (first entry) would pass most pages
findings.suggestion: Trivial, high-value unit tests with fixtures including \n/\f runs, no-English entries, and 0 values.

findings.issue: Alternate-form exclusion and type-slot ordering on the home page depend on the speciesIds set and per-species type maps; a subtle change (e.g. trusting type.pokemon ids directly) would reintroduce forms >10000 into lists
findings.suggestion: Test the species-mapping step with a fixture containing a >10000 id and slot-2 types.

findings.issue: Hidden-ability aggregation (existing.hidden ||= item.is_hidden) and the '<count> Pokémon' number are untested; a refactor could double-count Pokémon appearing in both slots or lose the hidden flag
findings.suggestion: Fixture-based test asserting count, ordering by dex number, and the 'Hidden ability' card text.

findings.issue: EvolutionTree/EvolutionBranch recursion and the nested-list shape for branching chains (Eevee) have no coverage beyond whatever the acceptance suite checks
findings.suggestion: Snapshot-free structural test (roles/nesting) of the rendered list for a branching chain fixture.

findings.issue: Dedup-by-id and dex-number sort of type Pokémon, plus the six damage-relation terms with 'None' fallback, are unguarded
findings.suggestion: Fixture tests for a relation with no entries and a list containing duplicate/alternate-form ids.

summary: The app ships zero tests of its own — no runner, no script, no spec files — so every risky area (home filtering/pagination/URL state, moves-table grouping and sorting, the fetch/cache layer, and the pure format helpers) is protected only by the externally-supplied acceptance suite. The good news is the riskiest logic is concentrated in small, pure, easily testable functions (lib/format.ts, compareRows, buildHref, the move-grouping block), so a lean Vitest suite would buy substantial regression safety cheaply. As it stands, a data-layer refactor could break filtering, ordering or not-found handling with no failing test in the repo.
